analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Higher oil prices revived persistent-inflation worries. Brent rose +4.07% to $104.28/bbl at the close, its biggest daily jump in two weeks, after peaking near $106/bbl intraday. It fell below $103 this morning after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms.

Escalation fears drove the oil move: Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports, fresh attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, and an Atlantic report that the White House asked the Pentagon for strike options usable before the midterms.

Both sides acknowledged US-Iran talks. Trump cited 'productive discussions' and Iran's Araghchi said Iran is reviewing a US proposal and will respond within days. Investors still priced a longer disruption into next year, with the December 2027 Brent future up +1.24% to a new high of $83.84/bbl.

European rates sold off at the front end. The 1yr Euro inflation swap rose +14.7bps to 3.49%, 10yr bunds rose +1.9bps to 3.49%, 10yr OATs rose +2.8bps to 4.89%, and 10yr gilts rose +3.7bps to 5.48%, a post-2007 high. The Franco-German 10yr spread held near 140bps.

Lagarde reportedly told Eurozone finance ministers the ECB has instruments to deal with unwarranted and disorderly market dynamics. DB calls this the first sign of soft verbal intervention by the ECB President.

US Treasuries recovered intraday. The 10yr yield hit 5.35% before closing down -5.7bps at 5.23%, helped by Trump's comments, the oil pullback and a solid 30yr auction. Waller said further Fed hikes 'do not need to come at consecutive meetings'.

DB sees a tension between financial stress, which raises doubts about more hikes, and persistent inflation, which pushes for tightening. In 2022-23 each stress episode (Ukraine invasion, Sept/Oct 2022 equity lows, SVB) caused a dovish repricing that proved premature as inflation reasserted itself. At the close, 69bps of further Fed hikes were priced by the June 2027 meeting and 61bps of ECB hikes.

Equities fell on both sides of the Atlantic. The S&P 500 fell -0.47% for a second straight decline, led by the Magnificent 7 (-0.95%), though two thirds of constituents rose. The STOXX 600 (-0.75%) hit its lowest since June, the CAC 40 (-0.51%) its lowest since March, and the STOXX Banks index (-2.26%) its lowest since June.

Chip stocks led US losses. The Philly semiconductor index fell -3.39%, its worst day in over 3 weeks, after the FT reported OpenAI's annualised revenue is about $50bn, below earlier reports near $70bn.

US initial jobless claims fell to 197k for the week ending October 3 (vs 200k expected). The 4-week average of 198k is the lowest since September 2022, when unemployment was 3.5%. Japan household spending fell -3.1% y/y in August, a ninth straight monthly decline.
Asia was mixed overnight: Nikkei -0.32%, Shanghai Comp -1.21%, CSI 300 -1.27%, Hang Seng +1.09%, ASX 200 +0.56%. S&P 500 futures are +0.30% and DAX futures +0.78% as oil keeps falling.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Claims came in below the 200k expected and the 4-week average is the lowest since September 2022, showing continued labour market resilience.
Due today. DB expects a reading near the prior one.
Markets still expect more Fed tightening, but at a slower pace than a couple of weeks ago.
Markets still expect further ECB tightening, less rapidly than before.
Up +14.7bps, its biggest daily jump in a couple of weeks, pushing yields higher at the front end.
Sharp intraday turnaround as oil eased and the 30yr auction was solid.

risk_factors: Further Middle East escalation, including strikes on Iran or attacks on Gulf shipping and infrastructure, could push oil higher.
Persistent inflation from higher oil could force more central bank hikes.
Tightening financial conditions and bond market stress, including gilts at post-2007 highs and OAT spread pressure.
AI-driven rally vulnerability if OpenAI revenue figures disappoint, weighing on chip stocks.
vol_and_positioning: iTraxx Crossover closed at 316, +8. iTraxx Europe was 64 (+1) and CDX 59 (+1).
Spreads were broadly steady even as European banks fell, with the STOXX Banks index -2.26%.
geopolitical: Houthi attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia and fresh attacks on ships through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Atlantic reported the White House asked the Pentagon to develop strike options on Iran usable before the midterms.
Trump posted that the US will not attack Iran before the Midterm Elections and is having 'productive discussions' with Iran.
Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran is reviewing a US proposal and will respond in the next few days (per Tasnim).

tension_points.theme: central bank hikes vs financial stress
tension_points.bull_case: Financial stress and tighter financial conditions are cutting expectations of future hikes, so Fed and ECB pricing is less aggressive than a couple of weeks ago and Waller said hikes need not come at consecutive meetings.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistent oil-driven inflation keeps pressure to tighten. In 2022-23 each dovish repricing proved premature as above-target inflation reasserted itself.

theme_stances.key_argument: In 2022-23 each stress-driven dovish repricing proved premature because above-target inflation reasserted itself.
theme_stances.evidence: above-target inflation eventually reasserted itself, so expectations for a dovish pivot proved repeatedly premature
